cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: A 7-step guide to running ads on ChatGPT
stories.plain: Early campaign data reveals how ChatGPT ads differ from Google or Meta — covering CPCs, targeting options, and measurement. This matters because marketers now have a live, practical guide to buying inside the dominant AI answer engine, which changes how paid media budgets are allocated and measured.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases updated Privacy Standards Portfolio for public comment
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab updated its Global Privacy Protocol and released Data Deletion Request Framework v2.0, open for comment until September 11. These standards set the interoperability rules that every CDP and ad platform must follow to stay compliant as US state privacy laws multiply — directly affecting how consent and deletion signals flow across the ecosystem.

stories.head: Wix launches Symphony, a standalone multi-agent system for SMBs
stories.plain: Wix released Symphony, a multi-agent AI platform that learns a small business's workflows and deploys a coordinated team of specialized agents to automate tasks and surface growth opportunities. It signals that agentic AI is moving from enterprise pilots to mainstream SMB tools, reshaping how small marketers build and run campaigns.

stories.head: Contentful's Palmata tool measures and corrects AI brand reputation in generative answers
stories.plain: Palmata monitors what AI engines actually say about a brand and flags inaccuracies, going beyond simple mention-tracking. This is an early product demo of AI answer accuracy management — a new GEO discipline where marketers must not only appear in AI results but ensure those results are factually correct.

stories.head: NiCE CTO on why AI pilots stall and how to govern agents proportionately
stories.plain: NiCE CTO Kevin Lee explains the organizational and technical reasons AI pilots fail to reach production, arguing for proportionate agent governance and knowing when a simple deterministic model beats a costly frontier LLM. Practical advice for anyone trying to move MarTech AI from demo to live deployment at scale.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: OpenAI has bolted product carousels and performance attribution onto ChatGPT ads, giving performance marketers the measurement plumbing they need to treat it as a real media buy rather than an experiment. This shifts ChatGPT from a curiosity to a channel that competes directly with Google and Meta for budget.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases updated privacy standards including GPP and Data Deletion Request Framework v2.0
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab has opened for public comment updates to the Global Privacy Protocol and a new Data Deletion Request Framework aimed at keeping ad tech compliant with a patchwork of state privacy laws. Marketers and platform builders have until September 11 to weigh in on rules that will shape how consent signals travel across the entire stack.

stories.head: A 7-step guide to running ads on ChatGPT: CPCs, targeting, and early performance data
stories.plain: The first hands-on breakdown of how ChatGPT ad campaigns actually behave — covering cost-per-click benchmarks, targeting options, and measurement gaps. Essential reading for anyone deciding whether to allocate budget to AI-native placements now or wait for the format to mature.

stories.head: How to manage AI prompt governance and costs at scale
stories.plain: Scaling generative content without cost blowouts or off-brand output requires centralized prompt libraries and token-budget controls. This practical framework covers who owns prompts, how to audit them, and how to tie spending to business outcomes — increasingly critical as AI content production moves from pilots to production.

stories.head: NiCE CTO Kevin Lee on why AI pilots stall before production and how to govern agents proportionately
stories.plain: NiCE's CTO explains the specific organizational and technical reasons most AI pilots never reach production, argues for proportionate rather than blanket governance, and makes the case for cheaper deterministic models over frontier LLMs for many marketing tasks. Practical framing for anyone trying to move past proof-of-concept.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: Conversational AI Becomes an Ad Inventory Channel
body: OpenAI is actively building ad-technology infrastructure, and early pilots like AdRoll's ChatGPT Ads program show that brands can now buy placements inside AI-generated answers. The search-and-discovery funnel is being restructured around conversational interfaces rather than keyword-ranked pages, which means paid and organic strategies must both adapt.

Practical guides to running ads on ChatGPT are already circulating, signalling that this is no longer experimental — it is an emerging media buy. Marketers who ignore conversational ad inventory risk ceding early-mover positioning in a channel that could rival traditional search advertising within two to three budget cycles.

themes.head: AI Rewrites Product Discovery & the Role of Publishers
body: AI recommendation layers, social commerce, and publisher-curated feeds are collapsing into a single moment of intent. The traditional funnel — awareness to consideration to purchase — is being compressed because AI surfaces specific products in the same breath as answering a question, bypassing brand-owned discovery touchpoints entirely.

For marketers, this means that being findable inside AI-indexed publisher content and social signals is as strategically important as paid search bids. Brands need structured data, rich product content, and media partnerships calibrated for algorithmic recommendation, not just human readers.

themes.head: From Pilot to Production-Scale AI: The Governance Gap
body: Multiple voices this month — NiCE's CTO, agency leaders at Ai4, and practitioners debating AI blind spots — converge on one problem: most organisations are still running AI as a series of disconnected pilots rather than governed production systems. Prompt sprawl, uncontrolled costs, and inconsistent outputs are the visible symptoms.

The fix requires treating AI like any enterprise software: version-controlled prompts, cost dashboards, clear ownership, and human-judgment checkpoints baked into workflows. Wix's Symphony multi-agent launch for SMBs shows that even lighter-weight operators now need structured orchestration rather than ad-hoc tool use.
ev: Agile Brand · NiCE CTO on pilot to production

themes.head: Privacy Standards Under Urgent Regulatory Refresh
body: IAB Tech Lab dropped a sweeping privacy-standards portfolio update for public comment, touching consent signalling, data clean rooms, and cross-channel compliance. These updates are not incremental — they reflect how AI-driven targeting has outpaced the consent frameworks that advertisers, publishers, and ad-tech vendors currently rely on.

Marketers need to track this public-comment window closely because the final standards will re-define what constitutes compliant audience activation. Organisations that wait for ratification before auditing their data flows will face expensive retroactive remediation — those that engage now can shape the rules to fit their stack.

MarTech Series · IAB Tech Lab announcement

themes.head: Human Judgment as a Competitive Marketing Skill
body: Counterintuitively, as AI automates execution, the skills rising in value are distinctly human: strategic framing, ethical reasoning, creative direction, and the ability to say no to fast but wrong decisions. Big Spaceship's CEO and Ai4 speakers explicitly argued that human judgment is the scarce resource, not compute or content volume.

Agencies are restructuring around this insight — moving from production-hour billing toward advisory and oversight roles where senior marketers set the guardrails that AI operates inside. This reframes AI not as a headcount replacement but as leverage that amplifies the judgment of skilled practitioners, making those practitioners more — not less — essential to hire and retain.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month — ad inventory, discovery, governance, privacy, and talent — AI is forcing marketers to make irreversible structural choices, not just tactical experiments, and the window to move deliberately rather than reactively is closing fast.
